subject: Crypto access patterns & retention — follow-up and clarifying questions
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Hall <simon.hall@fintrust.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-12T16:15:00Z
Subject: Crypto access patterns & retention — follow-up and clarifying questions

Hi Simon — great talk today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the next steps. I attached the short ops checklist and the call recording link.

Recap (from our discovery):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ mandatory, mutual TLS for some internal endpoints.
- At-rest: AES-256 envelope encryption. FinTrust prefers customer-managed keys (CMEK) where possible.
- Key custody: primary preference is HSM-backed CMK (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM through Redwood Private).
- Key rotation: you mentioned quarterly rotation; please confirm if monthly is required for compliance.
- Logging: key-usage logs and access audit trails required, retention requested is 13 months (you said >12 months).
- Residency: EU-only processing for customer-data buckets; audit logs can be stored in EU or mirrored for central ops.

Clarifying questions (so we can prepare authoritative guidance and an architecture diagram):
1) Can you confirm the required retention period for key-usage logs (13 months vs 24 months)?
2) Do you need per-tenant log separation, or is tenant-id tagging sufficient for your auditors?
3) For CMEK, are you open to a managed CloudKMS flow (Redwood holds wrapped-encryption keys with customer CMK in CloudKMS), or do you require the customer’s HSM to hold the master keys (no split key held by Redwood)?
4) Any hard requirement that the HSM be on-prem vs. cloud HSM (CloudHSM in eu-west vs on-prem HSM appliance)?

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Soojin (security) and Marissa (solutions) to cover CMEK options and logging playbook — 60 minutes.
- Share an architecture sketch and a short decision matrix comparing managed KMS vs BYOK with HSM plus the logging retention impact.

Proposed times: Thu 2028-09-14 09:00-10:00 CEST or Fri 2028-09-15 14:00-15:00 CEST — please pick one or suggest alternatives.

Attachments: redwood-kms-ops-checklist.pdf (ops summary), call-recording-url.txt (meeting recording link)

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

From: Simon Hall <simon.hall@fintrust.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-12T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Crypto access patterns & retention — follow-up and clarifying questions

Rafael — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and one ask from our side:

Answers:
- Retention: our compliance team has asked for 18 months for key-usage logs (we can push to 13 if you have an operational/cost reason, but 18 is the control they expect).
- Log separation: tenant-id tagging is acceptable, but logs must be tamper-evident and include immutable timestamps and request IDs.
- CMEK: preference is true BYOK where FinTrust controls the master key in an HSM we manage. CloudHSM managed by AWS is acceptable only if the HSM is provisioned in our dedicated AWS account and we control the key material lifecycle.
- On-prem HSM: desirable, but not a blocker if the cloud HSM path satisfies our control requirements.

Ask: can you provide any existing compliance evidence for the HSM/CloudKMS path (audit logs, sample key-usage report) and a short writeup of the envelope encryption flow you recommend? We need that for the internal procurement packet.

I'll take Thu 09/14 09:00 CEST for the deep-dive.

Regards,
Simon Hall
Head of Cloud Security | FinTrust Bank
simon.hall@fintrust.com

Thanks for the ping, Rafael. Quick draft reply items we can take into the deep-dive and also attach to procurement packet:

1) Envelope encryption flow (summary):
- Data path: Customer plaintext -> application-layer envelope encrypt (DEK) -> DEK wrapped by CMK (CMEK) in customer's KMS/HSM -> wrapped DEK stored alongside ciphertext in object metadata.
- Runtime key access: Serving runtime retrieves wrapped DEK, calls KMS/HSM in customer's account (or on-prem) to unwrap, uses unwrapped DEK in memory only, then drops DEK from memory after use.
- Controls: mutual TLS for KMS calls, strict IAM roles with short-lived credentials, customer-controlled key policies, and enforced key-usage audit logging.

2) HSM/CMEK options matrix (short):
- Option A (fastest): Redwood-managed KMS + envelope encryption. Pros: low ops overhead, predictable latency; Cons: customer does not control master key lifecycle.
- Option B (recommended for FinTrust): BYOK with CloudKMS/CloudHSM in customer's AWS account. Pros: FinTrust retains key control; Cons: integration complexity, cross-account IAM.
- Option C (highest control): On-prem HSM via Redwood Private. Pros: full customer custody; Cons: highest ops cost and longer lead time.

3) Logging & retention:
- We can provide tamper-evident key-usage logs (append-only storage with checksums) and support tenant-id tagging. Retention configurable per-account; 18 months is supported but note cost delta vs 13 months. I'll include estimated retention cost per TB in the matrix.

4) Evidence we can share:
- Sanitized key-usage sample (redacted timestamps/IDs) – safe to share.
- SOC 2 control summary referencing KMS usage (we can share the relevant control excerpt under NDA).
- Short envelope-encryption diagram (attach kms-options-matrix.xlsx).

I'll prepare the 1-pager and the matrix and upload to the shared drive before the deep-dive. Rafael — once I have the materials, I suggest we circulate a 2-slide pre-read to Simon so procurement has something to file.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Security Lead | Redwood Inference
